newsitem.title: USA: Diet change can cut breast cancer risk-U.S. report.
newsitem.headline: Diet change can cut breast cancer risk-U.S. report.

text.p: A specific diet can change breast tissue composition in a way that may reduce the risk of breast cancer, according to a study reported in the Journal of the U.S. National Cancer Institute on Wednesday.

American women might be able to reduce their risk of breast cancer by adopting a Japanese-style diet rich in vegetables, fish oils and soy products, the study at the University of California's Jonsson Cancer Centre here said.

"At least one aspect of human breast composition in American women can be altered to approximate the breast composition of women in certain Asian and European countries...(where) the indicence of breast cancer is much lower," Dr. John Glaspy, senior author of the study, said in a statement.
"We are very optimistic about these results. It's too early to make predictions, but we have absolute evidence that leads us to be optimistic," Glaspy said.

Glaspy studied 25 women with breast cancer who adopted a three-month diet heavy in soy products, fish oils and a variety of vegetables including grean leafy vegetables, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, cauliflower and carrots.
The women experienced an increase in a certain kind of polyunsaturated fatty acids, shown to reduce breast cancer risk, and a drop in other fatty acids known to promote cancer.
